revisits.item: Far from the (i) ___ her opponents had predicted, the minister's reply was a model of restraint for its first ten minutes. Only when a heckler accused her of lying did she abandon her notes, and even then her anger read less as calculation than as the reaction of someone (ii) ___ at being charged with the very dishonesty she had spent her career exposing. · blank 1: qualm / tirade / paradigm; blank 2: surly / halcyon / indignant
revisits.change: new sentence logic: a contrast instead of a cause, or a concession instead of a restatement

revisits.item: The first party to attempt the canyon expected the rock to be its chief danger and was half right. The river's channel proved so (i) ___ that every few hundred yards the crews had to line the boats by hand around another bend, and the walls, though sound enough never to threaten collapse, had been polished so smooth by floods that they gave the men bracing against them no (ii) ___ at all. · blank 1: turbid / intermittent / sinuous; blank 2: morass / purchase / declivity
revisits.change: new format: an SE item becomes a TC blank, or a TC blank becomes an SE pair

revisits.item: The old backpackers' rule, eat where the locals eat, was only ever a (i) ___ device: a quick way of narrowing the choices in a strange city, not a promise of a good meal. A recent essay sets out to (ii) ___ it, observing that locals crowd plenty of mediocre places out of habit or thrift. Yet the essay's deeper quarrel is (iii) ___ rather than culinary, since what it really asks is how a traveler with no palate for the cuisine could tell whose judgment to trust in the first place. · blank 1: illusionistic / heuristic / formalist; blank 2: substantiate / emulate / problematize; blank 3: phenomenological / epistemological / intertextual
revisits.change: a different SE partner or a different sense of the word

revisits.item: Had anyone thought to compare the ages of the two groups, the reviewers argued, the correlation the paper celebrated would have been exposed as not so much tenuous as ___; they took care, however, never to suggest that the authors had been anything other than scrupulous. · choices: tenuous / duplicity / spurious / efficacious / insincerity / bogus
revisits.change: a new context and no distractor shared with the earlier item
